solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 32 across, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: Republican gets outside division for tactical purposes

indicators.note: one word getting another outside it means the second wraps round the first

blocks.note: to cop is to catch or get, so 'gets' is COPS
standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician wins over a breakaway faction for strategic reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' reads as the verb of the sentence, but it is the outer word COPS, with R placed inside to give CORPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a military formation of several divisions, organised as one tactical unit.

clue.text: Pussies around with perishing asymmetrical boxes

indicators.note: something perishing disappears, so that letter is removed
around means encircling, so the animal word goes outside the rest

blocks.note: pussies are cats
skew means slanting or lopsided
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Cats curl round lopsided boxes that are falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is the letter W here, and 'perishing' kills it off. 'Pussies' is the outside, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Caskets are small decorative boxes for jewels or valuables, and in America coffins.

clue.text: Those struggling to get round runs with gross men

indicators.note: things struggling are in disorder, so the letters are jumbled
getting round something means enclosing it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
rank means gross or flagrant, as in rank stupidity

explanation.surface: Struggling troops go round in circles with crude companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' alone is the definition, in its army sense of soldiers below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: In military use 'men' means soldiers who are not officers, which is what other ranks are.

clue.text: We believe in bull! Photograph is bordering on tackiness

indicators.note: the border of a word is its edge, so only its outer letters are taken

blocks.note: to pap is to photograph like a paparazzo
taken as written
outer letters of tackiness

explanation.surface: A paparazzo photograph is shown to be tacky nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' looks like slang for nonsense, but it is the papal bull, a formal decree of the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Papists, a hostile term for Roman Catholics, accept the authority of the Pope who issues bulls.

clue.text: Listen to little Cecilia being a crybaby about Canada

indicators.note: listening means taking the word by ear, not by its spelling

blocks.note: Cissie is a pet form of the name Cecilia

explanation.surface: A young girl called Cecilia keeps whining about Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About Canada' does not wrap anything: it marks the spelling with S as the North American one, against British cissy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sissy is a timid, weak or effeminate person, close to a crybaby who cries easily.

clue.text: You and I did set about care for drunk

indicators.note: to be set about something is to surround it, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: 'you and I did' contracts to WE'D
to reck is an old verb meaning to care or heed

explanation.surface: Two people ganged up on someone over the cost of looking after a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Reck is an archaic verb, surviving mainly in 'reckless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrecked is slang for very drunk, as with smashed or hammered.

clue.text: Strain with stack

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
a rick is a stack of hay or straw

explanation.definitionFit: To wrick, also spelt rick, is to sprain or twist a joint, which is a strain.

clue.text: At sea tear around strait in ____?

definitions.text: At sea tear around strait in ____?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go outside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a gat is a channel or strait, a narrow passage of water

explanation.surface: Boats racing at sea tear through a narrow channel during the event.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank asks you to name the event that fills the picture; the whole clue describes boats racing round a channel while also giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat or yacht races, where crews tear round at sea.

clue.text: Company on top of peelie-wally Scottish mason

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
peelie-wally is Scots for pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: A firm headed by a pallid-looking Scottish stonemason.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on top of' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a cowan is a dry-stone builder who never served a proper mason's apprenticeship.

clue.text: New Yorker hiding upper-class and rude sort of sign for SA carrier

indicators.note: a new form of the word means its letters are remade in a different order
hiding things means keeping them inside, so the letters go within

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
U denotes upper-class usage
a V-sign made with the back of the hand is a rude British gesture

explanation.surface: A New Yorker hides a posh but offensive placard for a South African airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Yorker' reads as a city dweller, but New is the signal and YORKER the letters, rearranged around U and V.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa a kurveyor was a transport rider, someone who carried goods by ox-wagon.

clue.text: In a different way hold tip of little Indian plant

indicators.note: a different way of ordering means the letters are rearranged
the tip of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
first letter of little

explanation.surface: Instructions to grip a small Indian plant differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Dholl is the pigeon pea, a leguminous shrub grown in India for its edible seeds.

clue.text: I more or less agree: trade show finally made almost nothing

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word made
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a trade fair is a show for businesses
last letter of made
nought is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A grudging concession that a trade show ended up making next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUGHT loses its last letter to NOUGH, and FAIR + E + NOUGH gives FAIR ENOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'fair enough' is an idiom of reluctant or partial acceptance of a point.

clue.text: Panel identifying grasses within hedging west of green

indicators.note: the west end of a word written across is its first letter
a hedge surrounds a field, so hedging means enclosing what follows

blocks.note: to grass or shop someone is to inform on them to the police
within means in
first letter of green

explanation.surface: A display panel identifies the grasses growing in a hedge beside the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasses' looks botanical but is the British slang verb for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop sign is a board over a shopfront naming the business, so a panel that identifies it.

clue.text: Outdoorsy sort's ruthless shriek of disbelief

blocks.note: fell means cruel or ruthless, as in one fell swoop
Walker! or Hookey Walker! is an old exclamation of disbelief

explanation.surface: A hiker's cruel scream of incredulity.
explanation.walkthrough: Walker as an interjection is old slang of the 'tell that to the marines' kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellwalker hikes over fells, the hills of northern England, which is an outdoorsy pastime.

clue.text: Some dislike pistols such as are issued to legionnaires?

definitions.text: such as are issued to legionnaires

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their letters is taken

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word break dislikE PIStols

explanation.surface: Some people dislike the pistols handed out to soldiers of the Foreign Legion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rides on 'such as': things like those issued to legionnaires, with the question mark pointing to the hats rather than the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Kepis are flat-topped peaked military caps, famously worn by the French Foreign Legion.

clue.text: Clear about loading up a very light ship

indicators.note: about suggests turning around and rearranging, so the letters are reordered
loading means taking cargo on board, so the outer word takes the rest inside

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear up after loading a very light vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEAR is rearranged to CAREL and A V goes into its middle: CAR(AV)EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravel was a small, fast, light sailing ship used by Spanish and Portuguese explorers.

clue.text: Parrot in Iowa finds fertiliser in grainy clumps

blocks.note: Poll is a traditional name for a parrot
taken as written
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: A parrot in Iowa discovers lumpy fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fertiliser' sounds like farm manure, but it is the pollen that fertilises plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollinia are coherent masses of pollen grains, as in orchids, carried whole to fertilise another flower.

clue.text: This signals the end in recognised lines for wife

indicators.note: X for Y means X takes the place of Y within the word

blocks.note: knew means recognised
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife's lines in a play mark the closing scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In KNEW, the W is swapped for LL, giving KNELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the tolling of a bell for a death, so it announces an end.

clue.text: Thoughtlessly bring forward old hag until stopped

indicators.note: a stopped bottle has something plugged inside it, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: an old trout is a disparaging term for an unpleasant old woman
to means until, as in nine to five

explanation.surface: A careless push forward of an old woman until someone stops it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old trout' is an affectionately rude British term for an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot out an excuse or idea is to produce it again in a stale, unthinking way.

clue.text: Free security force switch around English

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the verb goes outside the abbreviation

blocks.note: UN peacekeepers act as an international security force
to switch is to whip or lash
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Release the guards and change round the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like changing over, but it is a whip, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to let loose, setting free something restrained.

clue.text: Hurdle made from bundle containing sort of thorn

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside, so the letter sits within the word

blocks.note: a bale is a bound bundle, of hay for instance
thorn is the Old English letter for th, later written like a Y, as in 'Ye Olde'

explanation.surface: A fence panel woven from a bundle of thorny branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thorn' looks like a plant, but it is the old runic letter. Y goes inside BALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayle is an old word for a barrier or palisade, a hurdle-like fence.

clue.text: Before lunch tug made fast to a vessel carrying oil

blocks.note: am is the morning, before midday
to tug is to pull
taken as written

explanation.surface: A morning tugboat is tied to an oil tanker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tug' and 'vessel' paint a harbour scene, but the vessel is a flask, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampulla is a small flask, used in church to hold holy oil.

clue.text: Boozer covered with weird secret principles rarely seen

indicators.note: covered with means wrapped by another word on the outside

blocks.note: eery is a variant spelling of eerie, weird
a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A drunk hides behind bizarre arcane beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: The weird word takes the older spelling without the I. 'Rarely seen' marks the answer itself as a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Esotery is a rare form of esotericism, doctrines kept for a select inner circle.

clue.text: Wit, for example, endlessly gives us sauce

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so each word loses its final letter

blocks.note: salt means pungent wit, as in Attic salt
say means for example

explanation.surface: A witty person, for example, keeps giving us cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: SALT and SAY both lose their ends. 'Sauce' wants to mean impudence in the surface but is the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy Mexican-style sauce of tomatoes, onion and chilli.

clue.text: Society ladies blocking a turn that's no laughing matter to SNP

indicators.note: to block something is to surround and shut it in
a turn faces everything the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
ladies are women
taken as written

explanation.surface: Society ladies blocking a stage act that the Scottish National Party finds unfunny.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside WOMEN between E and N, S is put in front, and SWOMEAN reversed gives NAE MOWS. SNP stands for Scots here.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, nae means no and mows means jokes, so nae mows is no joking matter.

clue.text: Illuminated fragment of long-forgotten literature

indicators.note: a fragment is only a piece, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters across the join forgottEN LITerature

explanation.surface: An illuminated page surviving from a forgotten manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illuminated' suggests medieval manuscripts, fitting the surface, but here it simply means lit up.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlit is a rare poetic past participle meaning lit up or kindled, so illuminated.

clue.text: Dramatically pay for supermarket having shifted head south

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving the head south sends the first letter to the bottom

blocks.note: Tesco is a major British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: Someone pays for the shopping at a supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatically' means as used in drama: Shakespeare has escot in Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Escot is a Shakespearean verb meaning to pay for or maintain someone.

clue.text: Japan topped this perfect winner

indicators.note: topped means having its top cut off, and the top of a down entry is its first letter

blocks.note: Nippon is the Japanese name for Japan

explanation.surface: Japan beat this flawless champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped' reads as beat, but it means beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo an ippon is a full point, a perfect score that wins the contest outright.

clue.text: Bung something to barbecue into the edges of it

indicators.note: into means placed inside another word

blocks.note: a rib is a cut of meat for grilling
'it' is the word barbecue, whose outer letters are B and E

explanation.surface: Throw a piece of meat on the barbecue, right to the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bung' looks like the verb throw, but it is the British slang noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is British slang for a bribe, an illicit payment.

clue.text: Robust article leaked

blocks.note: A is the indefinite article
to bleed is to leak, as ink does

explanation.definitionFit: Abled means able-bodied, fit and strong, so robust.

clue.text: Captain and dancer sleep in a dosshouse

blocks.note: first meaning: the master of a ship or team
second meaning: one who skips about
third meaning: a slang verb for sleeping rough or in cheap lodgings

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: the last is a verb, so the clue reads like a story of a captain and a dancer bedding down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a ship's master, someone who skips, and in slang means to doss down in a rough lodging.

clue.text: Established moot objection about Israel

indicators.note: about means around, so the word encircles the abbreviation

blocks.note: but is an objection put forward, as in no buts
IL is Israel's international code

explanation.surface: A long-standing objection raised in debate concerning Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moot' just colours the objection as debatable; IL is the international vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built has been set up or founded, which is to say established.

clue.text: Strike across difficult one in the manner of later batsmen?

definitions.text: in the manner of later batsmen

indicators.note: a word stretched across others lies on either side of them

blocks.note: a strike or take is a capture, as in 'take a wicket'
ill can mean hard, as in ill to please
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cricket strike-rate grumble about the lower order finding it hard.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the tail is the weak lower-order batsmen who come in last.
explanation.definitionFit: Taillike means resembling a tail, and the tail is cricket's term for the batsmen who come in last.

clue.text: Berlin's too easily seen as a feature of some nights out

definitions.text: a feature of some nights out

indicators.note: easily suggests loosely and freely, so the letters are treated as movable

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Berlin is a city whose nightlife is all too easy to spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nights out' sounds like clubbing, but it means nights spent outdoors under the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion's Belt is the row of three bright stars in Orion, easily visible on clear nights.

clue.text: Tense old dog circling new block

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the old word is placed around the abbreviation

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
rach is an obsolete word for a hunting dog
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A nervous elderly dog runs round a fresh block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside RACH to make RANCH, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranch, more often tranche, is a slice or portion, which is a block of something.

clue.text: What gets Disgusted going? Unsubstantial sort of food

indicators.note: what gets a word going is its start, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: first letter of Disgusted
airy means insubstantial, lacking weight

explanation.surface: An outraged letter-writer complains about flimsy fare; 'Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells' is the stock British name for such a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy is used attributively and as a noun for milk-based foods such as cheese and butter.
